The following chunks are only evaluated if the file `data/check_log.csv` exists.

```{r}
#| label: setup-check-log
#| eval: !expr file.exists("data/check_log.csv")
library(tidyverse)

interval_min <- 15                       # schedule: one run every 15 minutes
runs_per_day <- 24 * 60 / interval_min   # = 96

check_log <- read_csv("data/check_log.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    ts   = with_tz(as_datetime(run_at_utc), "Europe/Vienna"),
    date = as_date(ts)
  )

# Executed vs. scheduled runs
first_ts <- min(check_log$ts)
last_ts  <- max(check_log$ts)
executed <- nrow(check_log)
expected <- floor(as.numeric(difftime(last_ts, first_ts, units = "mins")) / interval_min) + 1
exec_pct <- round(executed / expected * 100, 1)

# Outcome of the executed runs
n_pass   <- sum(check_log$overall == "PASS")
n_fail   <- sum(check_log$overall == "FAIL")
pass_pct <- round(n_pass / executed * 100, 1)

# Runs per day; first and last day are only partly covered
first_day <- min(check_log$date)
last_day  <- max(check_log$date)

daily <- check_log %>%
  mutate(overall = factor(overall, levels = c("PASS", "FAIL"))) %>%
  count(date, overall, name = "runs", .drop = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(partial = date %in% c(first_day, last_day))

avg_full_day <- daily %>%
  filter(!partial) %>%
  group_by(date) %>%
  summarise(runs = sum(runs), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(avg = round(mean(runs))) %>%
  pull(avg)
```

## How many scheduled runs actually happened?

The collector was scheduled to run every `r interval_min` minutes. Between
`r format(first_ts, "%d %b %Y, %H:%M")` and `r format(last_ts, "%d %b %Y, %H:%M")`
(Vienna time) this corresponds to about `r expected` runs. The log contains only
`r executed` runs, i.e. `r exec_pct`% of the schedule. On the days that are fully
covered, on average only `r avg_full_day` runs per day were recorded, compared with
the `r runs_per_day` that a perfectly regular schedule would produce. Missing runs
are therefore not an exception but the normal case. This is consistent with the
fact that GitHub may delay or drop scheduled workflows when its servers are busy,
so the schedule should be read as "at most every `r interval_min` minutes", not as
a guarantee.

## What does the 100% PASS mean?

```{r}
#| label: pass-share
#| eval: !expr file.exists("data/check_log.csv")
check_log %>%
  count(overall, name = "runs") %>%
  mutate(share_pct = round(runs / sum(runs) * 100, 1))
```

Of the `r executed` runs that were executed, `r n_pass` passed all checks
(`r pass_pct`%) and `r n_fail` failed. This share only describes runs that
actually took place. A scheduled run that never started leaves no entry in the
log, so a high pass rate does not show that no data were missed. To judge
completeness, the pass rate has to be read together with the coverage of
`r exec_pct`% reported above.

```{r}
#| label: failed-checks
#| eval: !expr file.exists("data/check_log.csv")
#| results: asis
failed <- check_log %>%
  filter(overall == "FAIL") %>%
  separate_rows(failed_checks, sep = ";") %>%
  count(failed_checks, sort = TRUE, name = "times")

if (nrow(failed) == 0) {
  cat("**No failed runs.** All executed runs passed every check.\n")
} else {
  cat("Failed runs by the check that caused them:\n\n")
  cat(knitr::kable(failed, format = "markdown"), sep = "\n")
}
```

## Runs per day

```{r}
#| label: runs-per-day
#| eval: !expr file.exists("data/check_log.csv")
#| fig-alt: "Bar chart of collector runs per day, with a dashed line at 96 expected runs"
ggplot(daily, aes(x = date, y = runs, fill = overall, alpha = partial)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = runs_per_day, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate(
    "text", x = first_day, y = runs_per_day,
    label = paste0("expected: ", runs_per_day, " runs/day"),
    hjust = 0, vjust = -0.6
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(PASS = "#2a9d8f", FAIL = "#e76f51"), drop = FALSE) +
  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = c(`FALSE` = 1, `TRUE` = 0.45),
    labels = c(`FALSE` = "full day", `TRUE` = "partial day")
  ) +
  scale_x_date(date_labels = "%b %d", date_breaks = "1 day") +
  expand_limits(y = runs_per_day * 1.1) +
  labs(
    title = "Collector runs per day",
    x = NULL, y = "Runs", fill = NULL, alpha = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The first day (`r format(first_day, "%d %b")`) and the last day
(`r format(last_day, "%d %b")`) are only partly covered by the observation
period, so their bars are lower and shown in a lighter shade. They should not be
read as days on which the scheduler failed. The dashed line marks the 96 runs
per day expected at one run every `r interval_min` minutes; the gap between the
bars of the full days and this line is the number of skipped or delayed runs.

## Self-test: does the failure branch work?

A log that only ever shows PASS can also mean that the checks are too weak. The
chunk below runs the failure analysis on a small artificial log in which two
runs fail, to show that the code does report failed checks. To test the real
checks, make your script fail on purpose once (for example by pointing it to a
wrong URL) and look for a FAIL entry in `data/check_log.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: failure-selftest
#| eval: !expr file.exists("data/check_log.csv")
test_log <- tibble(
  overall = c("PASS", "FAIL", "FAIL"),
  failed_checks = c(NA, "row_count;no_missing", "row_count")
)

test_log %>%
  filter(overall == "FAIL") %>%
  separate_rows(failed_checks, sep = ";") %>%
  count(failed_checks, sort = TRUE, name = "times")
```
